name: pi0 failure recovery skill library
built_from: failure_agent_prototype/failure_survey (87 failures: libero_10 x5, libero_90 x82 from the 45-task survey split; video only). Per-episode detail: documentation/survey_results.json
supersedes: 0.1-poc (Documentation/failure_survey_test/skill_library); HL-1, HL-2, LL-1 keep their IDs and meaning

split_guard.note: only survey-split libero_90 tasks may be used for RL envs, reset states or demos

status_legend.proposed: derived from the survey, not yet run in closed loop
status_legend.validated: recovery succeeded when replayed from the recorded onset state

observation_budget: FR agent sees the agentview frame at 1 fps plus proprioception (EE pose, gripper width); no privileged sim state

levels.high: Reasoning error: wrong object, wrong destination, wrong skill or fixture, wrong spatial relation, wrong subtask order, or idling/never starting the next subtask. Recovered with primitives (HALT, RETREAT, POINT_APPROACH, REPROMPT, ...).
levels.low: Fine motor control or fine spatial perception: grasp misalignment, missed or slipped grasp, drop, a push/pull that stalls, a knob not turned far enough, an imprecise placement, knocking objects over. Recovered with an RL subtask policy (INVOKE_RL); instances carry onset and reset steps for rebuilding the scene from trace/states.npy.

disambiguation: HL-2 = wrong skill/fixture; HL-3 = wrong object category; HL-4 = right category, wrong instance (qualifier ignored); HL-6 = right object, wrong destination/relation. Each entry's detect.distinguish_from separates the remaining look-alikes.
camera_convention: agentview faces the robot: robot-left = IMAGE RIGHT, front = lower in the image (verified on libero_10/task4_success_init0)

HALT.effect: stop forwarding pi0 action chunks; send zero-delta actions to hold the EE pose

RETREAT.effect: scripted closed-loop OSC delta move of the EE in base frame using proprio only; gripper unchanged. Clears the contact/visual context that keeps pi0 stuck

REPROMPT.effect: resume pi0 with a new language instruction (pi0 replans every 5 steps, so it takes effect within 5 steps)

INSERT_SUBTASK.effect: edit the coordinator plan, e.g. put open(drawer) before place()

VERIFY.effect: VLM yes/no on a zoomed crop of the latest frame; true only if k consecutive 1 fps frames agree

WATCH.effect: keep monitoring at 1 fps for a cue; returns fired/not fired

INVOKE_RL.effect: hand control to an RL-finetuned subtask policy (low-level entries only, once trained)

ESCALATE.effect: give up on this entry: log it and ask the coordinator to replan

POINT_APPROACH.effect: VLM points at obj in the 1 fps agentview frame; back-project the pixel onto the table/fixture plane with the known camera calibration; scripted OSC move to dz above it; then hand control back to pi0. Images + calibration only, no privileged sim positions. New in v0.2: the v1 agent showed 'coordinator says WHERE, pi0 grasps' is the recipe that works, but used privileged positions (upper bound)

RELEASE.effect: scripted: lower 2 cm, open gripper, RETREAT up 10 cm. Fallback when pi0 will not let go

prompt_templates.note: pi0_libero has seen full LIBERO sentences, not bare atomic verbs. A bare 'pick up X' is out of distribution, so pick subtasks are phrased as complete pick-and-place sentences in the libero_spatial / libero_10 style.
prompt_templates.pick_place_on: pick up the {obj} and place it on the {dest}
prompt_templates.pick_place_in: pick up the {obj} and place it in the {receptacle}

entries.name: subtask_handoff_stall
entries.definition: pi0 completes a subtask (a fixture action or a successful grasp) and then idles; the next subtask never starts.
entries.applies_when: compound instruction, or a grasp that should be followed by transport; subtask k verified done; next target visible and not being approached

detect.proprio: EE displacement < 1 cm across 3 frames, OR EE out of camera view for 2 frames
detect.visual: VERIFY(done_subtask complete) == true AND EE not moving toward next_obj/next_dest
detect.distinguish_from: LL-7/LL-8 hesitation: there the EE is next to the *current* target making small adjustments; LL-1: current subtask not complete

entries.remedy_brief: VERIFY(prev done) -> HALT -> RETREAT 10 cm (back into view) -> REPROMPT next-subtask sentence -> WATCH 3 s; retry once -> ESCALATE

recovery.why: leave the finished fixture; also brings an out-of-view arm back into view

args.instruction: next-subtask sentence, e.g. pick_place_on(next_obj, next_dest); if an object is already held, the place sentence for it

recovery.on_not_fired: POINT_APPROACH(next_obj) + REPROMPT, retry once, then ESCALATE

entries.prevention: Coordinator issues one subtask at a time and advances only on VERIFY.
entries.success_check: VERIFY(next subtask started: EE at next_obj / object moving to next_dest) within 10 s

entries.name: scene_default_skill_override
entries.definition: pi0 runs the scene's habitual skill or fixture interaction (usually from a trained libero_10/libero_spatial task) instead of the instructed skill, e.g. pushes the open drawer shut, grabs a moka pot when told to turn the knob, skips the drawer and puts the bowl on the plate.
entries.applies_when: current subtask is skill S on target X, but the EE heads for a different fixture/object Y that belongs to a trained task in this scene

detect.proprio: EE path over 2 frames brings it closer to wrong_fixture and away from target, gripper empty
detect.visual: VLM: 'is the gripper approaching {target}?' == no AND 'is it at/pushing {wrong_fixture}?' == yes
detect.protected_state_check: VERIFY({protected_state}) every frame, e.g. 'top drawer is open'
detect.distinguish_from: HL-3: there the *skill* is right (pick-place) but the object is wrong

entries.remedy_brief: HALT -> RETREAT 10 cm + 5 cm from attractor -> INSERT_SUBTASK to restore any broken protected state -> POINT_APPROACH(target) -> REPROMPT object-first sentence -> WATCH 5 s; retry 15 cm -> ESCALATE

recovery.why: remove the attractor; pi0's skill choice is driven by what is near the gripper

args.instruction: object-first sentence for the instructed subtask

recovery.on_fired: repeat with RETREAT dz 0.15, then ESCALATE

entries.prevention: Declare protected states before running pi0. For fixture tasks (knob, drawer handle) POINT_APPROACH the fixture before the first pi0 step: the trained-task attractor wins within the first second.
entries.success_check: VERIFY(gripper at {target}) within 5 s AND protected_state still true

entries.name: wrong_object_category
entries.definition: pi0 grasps/moves an object of a different category than the target, typically one from a trained task in the same scene (alphabet soup instead of tomato sauce, white bowl instead of frying pan, mug instead of book).
entries.applies_when: subtask pick(target); gripper descending on / closing on an object

detect.proprio: pre-grasp trigger: EE z < ~5 cm above the support surface OR gripper width decreasing
detect.visual: VERIFY('the object between the fingers is the {target}', 2x crop around the gripper)
detect.distinguish_from: HL-4: same category, wrong instance (qualifier ignored)

entries.remedy_brief: pre-grasp VERIFY(object between fingers is target) -> HALT -> put wrong object back -> RETREAT 10 cm -> POINT_APPROACH(target) -> REPROMPT pick-place sentence -> VERIFY(grasped); retry -> ESCALATE

steps.why: set wrong_obj back down before moving on

recovery.why: re-prompting alone loses to the scene prior (the original prompt already did)

entries.prevention: Coordinator lists the scene's trained-task objects as known distractors; FR agent runs the pre-grasp VERIFY on every pick. In scenes that share objects with a libero_10 task, start with POINT_APPROACH rather than a plain prompt.
entries.success_check: VERIFY({target} grasped and lifted) within 10 s

entries.name: referring_expression_instance_error
entries.definition: Right kind of object or fixture, wrong instance: the qualifier (left/middle/right, colour, top/bottom drawer) is ignored. pi0 opens the middle drawer for 'top'/'bottom', always grabs the same book, takes the white mug for 'red mug'.
entries.applies_when: target is named with a qualifier and the scene has >1 instance of its category

detect.proprio: same pre-grasp / pre-pull trigger as HL-3
detect.visual: VERIFY phrased on the qualifier on a 3x zoom: 'is the gripper on the lowest handle?', 'is this the red mug?', 'is this the middle book?'

entries.remedy_brief: pre-grasp/pre-pull VERIFY phrased on the qualifier (3x zoom) -> HALT -> RETREAT -> POINT_APPROACH(resolved instance) -> REPROMPT -> VERIFY; retry -> ESCALATE

args.subtask: undo wrong_instance change, e.g. close the wrongly opened drawer

entries.prevention: The coordinator resolves the qualifier itself, in the robot frame (robot-left = IMAGE RIGHT; front = lower in the image; verified on libero_10 task4), and gives pi0 a pointed target, never the qualifier alone.
entries.success_check: VERIFY(correct instance grasped / correct drawer moving)

entries.name: intermediate_subtask_skipped
entries.definition: In a multi-step instruction, pi0 skips a middle subtask (e.g. the stack in 'stack A on B and place them in C') and carries a single object straight to the final destination. It never stacked in any surveyed episode.
entries.applies_when: instruction with an intermediate stack/combine subtask before the final place

detect.proprio: loaded gripper moving toward container before VERIFY(stacked)
detect.visual: VLM: 'is {top_obj} resting inside {base_obj}?' == no while the EE heads to {container}

entries.remedy_brief: HALT before the single object reaches the container -> stack in place if base already in container, else POINT_APPROACH(top) + REPROMPT stack sentence -> VERIFY(stacked) -> REPROMPT place sentence for the base

args.instruction: pick up the {top_obj} and place it on the {base_obj}

then.why: stacking in place satisfies the goal

args.instruction: pick up the {top_obj} and place it on the {base_obj}
pick up the {base_obj} and place it in the {container}

entries.prevention: Split 'stack and place' into two VERIFY-gated prompts.
entries.success_check: VERIFY(top_obj in base_obj AND base_obj in container)

entries.name: destination_misgrounding
entries.definition: pi0 holds the correct object but carries it to / hovers at / places it in a non-instructed destination or relation, usually the trained task's destination (back compartment for 'front', right of the plate for 'left of', microwave for 'in front of the mug'), or hovers without committing.
entries.applies_when: object grasped; subtask place(obj, dest, relation)

detect.proprio: loaded gripper moving away from the destination over 2 frames, OR hovering > 3 s without nearing it
detect.visual: VLM: 'is the held {obj} moving toward / above {destination} ({relation})?' == no
detect.distinguish_from: LL-7: the object is AT the correct destination but not released

entries.remedy_brief: HALT keeping grasp -> RETREAT up 10 cm -> POINT_APPROACH(destination point) -> REPROMPT place sentence or scripted lower-and-release -> VERIFY(on/in); retry -> ESCALATE

recovery.fallback: RELEASE if pi0 still will not lower

entries.prevention: The coordinator turns relation/compartment words into a target point before the carry; pi0 is not trusted with relations. 'Under the shelf' may need a horizontal-insertion skill (open gap from v1).

entries.name: target_never_approached
entries.definition: pi0 hovers/wanders among other objects and fixtures for the whole episode and never approaches the instructed target (e.g. a bowl in an unusual raised start pose on top of the microwave).
entries.applies_when: any subtask; no progress toward target after the first seconds

detect.proprio: EE-to-target distance (from VLM pointing) not decreasing over 3 frames
detect.visual: VLM heading check: 'is the gripper moving toward {target}?' == no for 3 frames
detect.distinguish_from: HL-2/HL-3: there pi0 commits to a specific wrong fixture/object

entries.remedy_brief: early heading check (2-3 frames) -> HALT -> RETREAT -> POINT_APPROACH(target) -> REPROMPT -> WATCH 3 s -> ESCALATE
entries.prevention: Heading check in the first 2-3 frames instead of waiting for the timeout.

entries.name: grasp_loss_unnoticed
entries.definition: After a missed or slipped grasp (LL-4/LL-5), pi0 continues the transport/place motion with an empty gripper instead of re-grasping.
entries.applies_when: after any pick; object no longer between the fingers

detect.proprio: gripper width ~0 (fully closed) while EE moves toward destination
detect.visual: VERIFY('{obj} is between the fingers', crop) == false
detect.distinguish_from: a deliberate release at the destination

entries.remedy_brief: post-grasp VERIFY(object between fingers, width > 0) fails -> HALT -> RETREAT 10 cm -> POINT_APPROACH(object) -> INVOKE_RL(rl/pick) or REPROMPT pick sentence -> VERIFY; retry -> ESCALATE
entries.prevention: VERIFY the grasp after every pick before allowing transport; this turns every LL-4/LL-5 into a recoverable event.

entries.name: drawer_push_stall
entries.definition: While closing a drawer pi0 pushes from above; the drawer travels 1/2-2/3 of the way, then the hand rests on the drawer front.
entries.applies_when: subtask close(drawer); drawer not flush; EE at drawer front

detect.proprio: EE displacement along the closing direction < 1 cm across 2 frames while at the drawer
detect.visual: VERIFY('{drawer} front is flush with the cabinet', 2x zoom) == false

recovery.status: proposed, expected weak (re-runs the same pi0 behaviour)

entries.name: knob_approach_contortion
entries.definition: Approaching a small fixture (a stove knob), the wrist/elbow folds into a twisted configuration, the wrist body touches the knob instead of the fingertips, and the arm swings away (often out of view) without turning it.
entries.applies_when: subtask turn_on/turn_off(stove); EE near the knob

detect.proprio: large wrist-joint rotation (> 90 deg) within 1 s near the knob, or EE leaves the view
detect.visual: VLM: 'are the fingertips on the knob?' == no while the wrist touches it
detect.distinguish_from: HL-2 in KITCHEN_SCENE8: there the EE never goes to the knob

recovery.status: proposed, expected weak (re-runs the same pi0 behaviour)

entries.name: unstable_grasp_slip
entries.definition: The grasp closes on a rim, edge or handle; during lift or transport the object tilts, pivots or slips out of the gripper (bowl rims, book top edges, mug rims, pan handles).

detect.proprio: gripper width drops to ~0 during lift/transport (object lost), or EE rises but obj stays
detect.visual: VLM on crop: 'is {obj} tilted / hanging / back on the table?'
detect.distinguish_from: LL-5: contact disturbance BEFORE a grasp forms
